steps.content: The familiar dizziness surges within you as specks of white light begin to flicker before your eyes. But this time you're not alone—the prodigious young herbalist from Eastia stands right behind you.
At least, that's what you think at first.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Aconite root, pokeweed, datura flower... Just a moment, my friend. This prescription is rather complex. It's quite potent precisely because of its toxic nature.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Combined with the time-based acupuncture technique, as long as we calculate the right acupoints at the proper hour, we can restore your Qi in no time...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Wait, did you just say the medicine is toxic?! And what's all this about needle techniques, proper hours, and calculating acupoints...?

As you watch Wuhuanzi close her eyes and begin making mystical calculations with her fingers, your already spinning head grows even dizzier. All her suspicious behaviors from your earlier exploration flash before your eyes.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: (She let herself get led away by some spirit who was obviously suspicious, volunteered for treatment only to make everything worse, and now she's using medicine made from what might as well be poisonous weeds from DisCity's gardens... I really might have asked the wrong person for help...)

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I've calculated which acupoints we need. Please, have a seat.

As your panic rises with each recollection, Wuhuanzi's ice-cold hand pats your shoulder. At this point, you have no other options... With a deep breath, you resign yourself to following the herbalist's instructions.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: This shouldn't hurt... You can ease yourself further. Should your muscles remain excessively taut, the task of the needles in accessing the acupoints might be impeded, potentially compromising the treatment's effectiveness.

For once, you're actually clear-headed while receiving this mysterious Eastian treatment, though doubt and unease still linger in your mind. Trying to distract yourself, you attempt to relax your muscles while starting a conversation.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'd say I'm pretty experienced with handling pain, so this is more like... nervousness, I guess. I mean, I've never had the pleasure of getting the same treatment as a spirit—is this a standard practice?

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Rather than a matter of standard practice... I'd say all afflictions—be they mundane or spiritual—are simply illnesses. For us practitioners of healing, there exist only two kinds: those we can cure, and those beyond our reach.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Even the entities you refer to as "spirits"—their madness, their twisted forms—all stem from illness. Where there is an illness, there lies the potential for remedy. And where healing is achieved, merit is gained.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So that's why you never shy away from them, even actively seeking them out to treat their illnesses, refusing to give up even when you might be deceived...?
Wuhuanzi nods.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: All this effort for what you call "merit"...? But those conditions you have been treating—they might already be at the terminal stage beyond saving.

As the medicinal concoction bubbles away, you observe Wuhuanzi skillfully inserting needles while you remain seated. Her expression retains its characteristic impassiveness—neither discouraged by failure nor seemingly aware of the subtle probing in your words.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Are you not the same, my friend? You willingly venture into the territory of "spirits" to save companions who may be beyond saving, strangers who might have already been devoured...

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: You stake your own vitality as collateral, treating your Qi as a disposable resource. Yet deep down, you know full well that herbalists are not miracle workers—I cannot wholly rejuvenate a body that has been constantly pushed to the brink of the "terminal stage."

The young herbalist from Eastia deftly pours the medicinal brew into a porcelain bowl and hands it to you. As you grimace at the visibly unpalatable concoction, her voice grows softer, watching you as if pondering something.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: To be honest, I've seen many who spurn treatment, harbor suspicions, question my intentions, or hold fast to the belief that mere healing cannot alter destiny... Yet, never have I crossed paths with someone like you, eagerly allowing me to "reap" merit from them.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: I can't help but wonder—perhaps my decoction isn't bitter enough?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Are you saying there are even more bitter medicines? Don't tell me I didn't need to drink something this bitter...

You wipe away the involuntary tears brought on by the medicine's pure bitterness, unable to hide your growing suspicion. Wuhuanzi, however, merely lowers her gaze, her lips tightening ever so slightly.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: Effective medicine often carries a bitter taste, yet increased bitterness doesn't equate to superior efficacy. If stronger bitterness truly meant better effect... I wouldn't mind even if you called me the Yama of Bitter Remedies.

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: ...If only it were that simple. Medicine remains just medicine in the end. There will forever be realms beyond its grasp, pains it cannot soothe. Perhaps that's what you meant by the "terminal stage."

steps.speaker: Wuhuanzi
steps.content: For now, all I wish... is to help you escape this place before that inevitable state befalls you. And if we can save others along the way... all the better.

There she goes again. You observe this young Eastian girl, whose eerie presence stands out even in this mystical street of spirits, as you silently finish the medicine. She always sees the worst, always speaks of the worst—struggling negatively while enthusiastically giving up.
From her cryptic words and contradictory actions, you can be certain of one thing: this young Sinner before you... must be harboring some hidden truth that drives her to act this way.
